svg.title: Stage 01 One-Sided Landau Funnel: Prime Ceiling to Critical Line
svg.desc: Two-panel editorial mathematical diagram of the Stage 01 one-sided reduction funnel. Left panel shows the smoothed prime remainder R_q0(x) = sum_{n <= x} lambda(n)(1/n - 1/x) - (log x)/phi(q0) - c_q0 with nonnegative weight lambda(n) = Lambda(n)(1 - (n/d)) on n = 1 (mod q0), plotted as an oscillating curve staying strictly underneath the dashed one-sided ceiling A x^(beta - 1) = A x^(-1/2 + epsilon) with no lower barrier required. Below the plot, the two-cutoff scale ladder x << x1 << b (x^(10^6) <= x1, (x1)^(10^6) <= b, log x1 >= x^(epsilon/12), m in [sqrt(x), 2 sqrt(x)]) shows classical PNT crushing |R_q0(x1)| and |R_1(x1)| <= x^(-2), yielding R_q0(y) <= (128 phi(q0) + 32) y^(-1/2 + epsilon) via New.eventually_primeRemainder_le_mul_rpow. Right panel shows the complex s-plane with critical strip 0 < Re(s) < 1, dashed critical line Re(s) = 1/2, Re(s) = beta > 1/2, Re(s) = 1, and the target zero-avoidance box {Re(s) >= beta, |Im(s)| <= |Im(rho)|} containing candidate point rho. Three numbered cards explain: (1) quadratic-twist selection (exists_entireL_quadTwist_ne_zero) choosing prime d = d0 (mod q0) so all twisted L(chi chi_d, s) satisfy n'(s) = 0 inside the box; (2) real-axis sign positivity with no no-real-zeros assumption, since on (beta, 1] both x(1-x) >= 0 and n(x) >= 0 give Re r(x) >= 0 while n(x) = 0 for x >= 1; and (3) Landau's lemma (IsPolar.landau) forcing r(rho) = 0, n(rho) = 0, and L(psi, rho) != 0, feeding New.grh and functional-equation reflection s -> 1 - s (New.zeros_on_line) onto Re(s) = 1/2. A compact bottom flow strip connects star_inequality to OneSidedBound to Criterion to New.grh to New.Main.
svg.text: Stage 01 One-Sided Landau Funnel: Ceiling to Critical Line

g.text: λ(n) = Λ(n)(1 − (n/d)) ≥ 0 on n ≡ 1 (mod q₀), else 0
Pick prime d ≡ d₀ (mod q₀) via zero-density bound
so all twisted L(χχd, s) satisfy n'(s) = 0 inside box.
On (β, 1]: x(1−x) ≥ 0 and n(x) ≥ 0 ⇒ Re r(x) ≥ 0.
For x ≥ 1: classical nonvanishing forces n(x) = 0.
Bound + Re r(x) ≥ 0 ⇒ r(ρ) = 0 ⇒ n(ρ) = 0 ⇒ L(ψ, ρ) ≠ 0.
Feeds New.grh & s ↦ 1−s (New.zeros_on_line) to Re(s) = ½.
